subject: Request: DPA carveout for SpectraHealth POC — signoff needed
messages:
From: Elaine Moore <elaine.moore@spectrahealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Rachel Singh <r.singh@spectrahealth.com>, SpectraHealth Legal <legal@spectrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA carveout request for Redwood POC (limited data use)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for running the POC next week — quick ask from our side before we kick off: our legal team needs a narrow DPA carveout for this initial pilot. Key points they want included in the redline (attached):

- Limited data use: data collected during the POC may only be used to operate the POC and for debugging; no model training or model improvement allowed.
- Retention: PII/PHI must be deleted within 30 days of ingestion.
- Subprocessors: please provide a full subprocessor list and confirm no new subprocessors will be engaged for the POC without prior notice.
- Runtime access scoping: SpectraHealth requires that runtime access be constrained to prefix-only KV/cache, not full request logs.

We attached our proposed DPA redline (SpectraHealth_DPA_redline_v1.docx) and a short diagram of the POC data flow. Our legal deadline to approve the POC is end of day Wednesday (48 hours). Can you loop in the right people at Redwood (product & security) for signoff?

Appreciate you moving quickly — if any of these items are blockers, tell me which ones and we can discuss tradeoffs.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Moore
Head of Data Partnerships | SpectraHealth
[Attachment: SpectraHealth_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: POC_scope_diagram.png (image)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA carveout request for SpectraHealth POC — need security + product review

Ben / Neha — forwarding SpectraHealth's proposed redline and POC diagram. TL;DR: they want a narrow DPA carveout for a 2-week POC: no-training clause, 30-day retention for PII/PHI, subprocessor assurances, and runtime access limited to prefix/KV only (no full request logs). Legal needs signoff by EOD Wed.

Questions for you:
- Ben: from Security's POV, can we accept the "no model training" clause for a POC and still provide the telemetry/logging they need for debugging? Any mandatory audit/KMS requirements we should flag?
- Neha: product/serving impact — limiting runtime access to prefix/KV only: what does that prevent (tracing/telemetry hooks)? Will this require a config change or degrade latency/observability?

Suggested next steps: Security to propose minimal evidence checklist (SOC2 control mapping + KMS/audit clauses) and Product to propose runtime config/controls and an estimate of dev effort if needed. If both green, I will send a counter-redline to SpectraHealth. Deadline: 2026-08-05 23:59 PDT.

Quoted message below.

--Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA carveout request for SpectraHealth POC — security notes

Thanks for the ping — read the redline. High level: security is supportive of a narrow POC carveout provided we get two things in writing and a small configurable change:

1) Technical controls and evidence:
   - KMS must be used for any key material and we need an explicit audit logging clause (immutable logs for at least 90 days accessible to Redwood security).
   - We will provide a short security evidence pack mapping the redline clauses to SOC2/ISO controls.

2) Subprocessor transparency:
   - We can share the current subprocessor list and commit to notify SpectraHealth of changes; however we cannot give an absolute guarantee of zero changes forever — suggest a 30-day prior notice clause for new subprocessors that would affect the POC.

3) Runtime scoping:
   - Constraining runtime access to prefix/KV only is reasonable; we should explicitly exclude request payload dumping and high-resolution request logs. We will need a Product/Engineering config flag to disable streaming traces for this tenant.

4) No-training clause:
   - Security has no objection to a temporary no-training clause for this POC, so long as telemetry required for debugging (error rates, aggregated performance metrics) is allowed in anonymized/aggregated form.

Timing: we can produce the evidence pack and proposed security addendum within 48 hours if Product confirms the runtime configuration requirement and a contact at Infra to implement the flag.

I attached a short checklist we use for DPA carveouts internally.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security_evidence_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA carveout request for SpectraHealth POC — product impact and suggested compromise

Thanks — quick product take after reviewing the POC diagram:

- Runtime scoping to "prefix/KV only": implementation is feasible but not entirely frictionless. Current runtime stores short-term KV caches and full request traces for debugging. To fully honor SpectraHealth's ask we need to:
  - Expose a per-tenant config to disable request-level tracing and streaming traces (engineering change, small backend flag + routing rule).
  - Ensure that the telemetry we keep is aggregated and anonymized (no raw payload snapshots). That will reduce observability for edge cases and may make debugging slightly slower.

- No-training clause impacts: our default analytics pipeline collects anonymized usage metrics for quality monitoring. We can neutralize model training/updates for this tenant and instead generate a separate aggregated report for SpectraHealth. Product needs 3 business days to implement the tenant flag and 1-day QA to validate deletion/retention behaviour.

Suggested language for the counter-redline (short):
  - "For the duration of the POC (dates X–Y), Redwood will not use SpectraHealth data to train model parameters or for model improvement. Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, anonymized telemetry for debugging and service quality monitoring; raw request payloads and user-identifiable data will not be stored beyond the retention window specified below."

If Security provides the evidence pack and Infra commits to the flag, I can draft the technical annex and an engineer estimate (3 days dev + 1 day QA). Let me know if Legal needs different wording for the telemetry carveout.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
